title: IC 4212
caption: The barred spiral galaxy IC 4212, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image shows IC 4212, a barred spiral galaxy in the constellation Virgo. It sits close to the celestial equator, so at certain times of year it can be seen, at least partly, from both hemispheres.

The celestial equator is the projection of Earth's equator onto the sky. Objects near it rise and set for observers both north and south of the equator, unlike objects near the celestial poles, which can only be seen from one hemisphere.

A barred spiral galaxy has a straight bar of stars across its center, with spiral arms extending from the ends of the bar. Bars are thought to help funnel gas toward a galaxy's center, where it can feed new star formation. The image was taken with the Dark Energy Camera on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, through g, r and z filters, as part of observations led by J. Moustakas of Siena College.
